To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
tourism specialization and competition exert a synergic impact on hotel industry efficiency, and that tourism specialization enhances the impact of competition on hotel efficiency.

(1) the efficiency of the Chinese hotel industry is affected by both specialization in tourism by a destination and market competition; (2) specialization in tourism by itself does not guarantee high levels of hotel efficiency; and (3) tourism specialization enhances the negative effect of competition on hotel efficiency.
tourism specialization and competition exert a synergic effect on the efficiency of hotel industry in China.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of tourism specialization and market competitiveness on the efficiency of hotel industry, and the results provide a useful reference for tourism policy makers and hotel managers in the hotel industry.
the effects of tourism specialization and market structure on hotel industry efficiency.
the relationship between tourism specialization and hotel industry efficiency.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
tourism specialization does not guarantee hotel efficiency but does make the negative effect of competition on efficiency worse.
the hotel industry is a highly efficient industry, which is not only driven by the level of tourism specialization of the province but also by the degree of market competition in the tourism market.
tourism development as measured by specialization in tourism does not guarantee high performance in hotels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hotel industry should be cautious when pursuing tourism development.
tourism development and tourism specialization do not necessarily enhance the efficiency of the hospitality industry.
tourism specialization and competition are both important factors that influence the hotel industry efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a tourism destination should be aware of the fact that a high degree of tourism specialization can lead to a high level of market competition and that this combination can have a negative impact on hotel efficiency.
the government should not overemphasize tourism specialization as a means of improving hotel industry efficiency.
tourism development should not only be focused on increasing the number of tourists and their spending in a destination but also on enhancing the efficiency of the tourism sector.
